tokyo_warabimochi_motoko_asaku.price_note: PARTIAL: the shop names its three warabimochi varieties and two drink formats on its own site and publishes NO PRICES, so every price field below is empty rather than guessed. Tabelog not consulted: Cf-Mitigated: challenge (403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ WARABIMOCHI IS ONE OF THE BEST JAPANESE SWEETS FOR BOTH DIETS AND IT DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON A WORD THE SHOP DOES NOT USE. True warabimochi is set from 本蕨粉 — BRACKEN ROOT STARCH — which is a fern rhizome: no wheat, no dairy, no egg, nothing animal, and it is dusted with きな粉 (roasted SOYBEAN flour) and eaten with 黒蜜 (cane syrup). On that construction it is plant and gluten-free outright. ⚠ BUT ALMOST NO COMMERCIAL WARABIMOCHI IS MADE THAT WAY. Bracken starch is scarce and expensive, so the overwhelming majority of shops use a blend of sweet-potato or tapioca starch — still wheat-free — and some use わらび餅粉 blends that include other starches. The shop says only 「原料、製法にこだわって作られる」, that it is particular about materials and method, which is a quality claim and not an ingredient one. It does not name 本蕨粉 anywhere. So the base is very likely wheat-free but is not declared, which is why these are "ask" rather than "gf". ⚠ AND THE DRINKS ARE THE OPPOSITE WAY ROUND: わらび餅ミルクティー and わらび餅ソフトクリーム are both DAIRY — the mochi is the plant part and the vehicle is not. The soft serve is Asakusa-only.

items.note: ⚠ THE BASE IS ALMOST CERTAINLY WHEAT-FREE AND IS NOT DECLARED. Warabimochi is set from bracken-root or other root starch — never wheat — and dusted with きな粉, roasted soybean flour. Both flags stay open because the shop names neither its starch nor whether the kinako or syrup carry anything else. If the answer comes back 本蕨粉, きな粉 and 黒蜜, this is a dessert that clears both diets.
The brown-sugar version. 黒糖 is unrefined cane sugar — plant.
Matcha is powdered green tea, plant and wheat-free in itself.

tokyo_korean_dining_sai.price_note: Complete lunch, dinner and take-out cards from the shop’s own site — だいにんぐ彩（サイ）, Korean home cooking at 台東区花川戸2-11-15, near Sensoji’s Nitenmon. Prices as printed; the site adds ＋100円 for a coffee or tea with lunch, and says further items appear on Tabelog (not reachable from this machine). Lunch 11:30-15:00 (L.O. 14:00), dinner 17:00-23:00 (L.O. 22:00), closed Sundays; take-out orders 11:30-15:00 and 17:00-20:00, with the 特製焼肉弁当 and オードブル requiring advance booking. ⚠ KOREAN HOME COOKING IS A SOY-SAUCE AND GOCHUJANG KITCHEN AND BOTH ARE WHEAT. Commercial gochujang in Japan is made with 小麦粉 as standard, so 石焼きビビンバ, ヤンニョムチキン, トッポギ, キムチ dishes, プデチゲ and チーズタッカルビ are all out unless the shop makes its own from rice — it advertises 自家製コチュジャン for the yangnyeom chicken but does not say what is in it, so that is an ask, not a clearance. ⚠ SEPARATELY THE LUNCH CARD IS HALF JAPANESE-WESTERN: ハンバーグ, 生姜焼き and カレーライス are all wheat (panko, soy-mirin glaze and roux respectively), and the three 煮込みうどん lines are wheat noodles by name. ⚠ CHAPCHAE IS THE ONE THAT SURPRISES PEOPLE: 春雨 sweet-potato glass noodles are naturally wheat-free, but chapchae is dressed in soy sauce, so it goes down on the sauce, not the noodle. What is left is thin: the チョレギサラダ (sesame-oil salad) and the plain rice, both still ask because no allergen statement is published.

tokyo_hana_to_gohan_to_cream_s.price_note: NO ITEMISED MENU EXISTS FIRST-PARTY. The only page anyone publishes for 花とごはんとクリームソーダ なぎさ食堂 is its listing in the Tokyo Dome City gourmet guide, in Japanese and English, and that page carries a description, hours, seat count, phone and a BUDGET BAND — lunch 1,000-2,000 yen, dinner 1,000-3,000 yen — but not one dish name or price. The listing has no link to any shop website; the shop’s contact number is a mobile (090-1221-7234). What the operator does say about the food: it is a 魚料理＆クリームソーダ shop (fish dishes and cream sodas) in the Meets Port area, 24 seats, 11:30-19:00 with last orders at 18:30, doing photogenic cream sodas and an afternoon tea, with alcohol in the evening. A fish-and-cream-soda kissaten in a Japanese food court is a soy-and-dashi kitchen by default and there is nothing published to check that against, so no items are recorded.

tokyo_sawawa_asakusa_chawawa.price_note: NO MENU IS PUBLISHED AND THE OPERATOR’S OWN PAGE IS STALE. 茶和々 浅草店 appears on 株式会社寺子屋’s corporate site as a bare shop-directory entry: name, phone (03-6231-6044), address (台東区浅草2-2-10), an empty shop-news slot, and 情報更新日：2020年4月20日 — an entry last touched in April 2020. There is no menu, no price, no product list for the shop. Telacoya is a souvenir-confectionery group (企画・製造・販売 across 直販, 特販, 通販 and its own sweets factory) and its 事業案内 page describes that structure without listing what any individual 茶和々 shop sells. Nothing about matcha sweets or warabi mochi at this address was read anywhere, so nothing is recorded.

tokyo_goo_italiano_shibuya_hon.price_note: NO MENU COULD BE READ, AND THE REASON IS THE PLATFORM RATHER THAN THE SHOP. The site for goo ITALIANO 渋谷本店 is built on STUDIO (studio.site), a Nuxt single-page app that ships an empty HTML shell and paints the page from JavaScript. curl and WebFetch both return only the site title and a STUDIO banner. This tick went further than a fetch: STUDIO publishes each site's content as a snapshot JSON in Google Cloud Storage, and the app's own __NUXT_DATA__ payload names the exact path. That snapshot was retrieved and parsed — and its "components" key is an empty object, so the text simply is not in the published payload this egress can reach. Menu subpaths (/menu, /food, /drink) were probed as well and either 404 or return the same shell. This is a COMPLETE result for a text-only harvest: the shop may well display a full menu to a real browser, but nothing was found that could be quoted, and nothing has been guessed. A future pass with a headless browser that executes JavaScript is the way to finish this record; a re-fetch will not be. ONE THING THE SNAPSHOT DID YIELD, and it is a gluten fact rather than a menu: the site's own meta description states 「特にgoo ITALIANOのパスタ料理はオススメで、パスタは南イタリアグラニャーノの伝統製法麺で長時間低温でじっくり乾燥させることで、モチっとした食感と小麦の香りが楽しめます」 — the house speciality is Gragnano dried pasta, and the shop itself advertises 小麦の香り, the aroma of the wheat. The kitchen's signature is durum wheat pasta. The snapshot also lists the site's page structure, which includes separate shibuya and yoyogiuehara modals, so a future visual pass must take the SHIBUYA one — this record is the 渋谷本店, not the Yoyogi-Uehara branch.

tokyo_tetchan_shinjuku.price_note: Prices from the shop's own HotPepper page, which trades as 「肉酒場 てっちゃん 新宿店」 at 新宿区新宿3-34-13 三経ビル7階 — the record's Shinjuku Sanchome placement. Note the prices on this card are printed WITHOUT a 税込 marker, unlike the rest of this operator's listings, so treat them as pre-tax until the counter says otherwise. ⚠ This is a meat izakaya and the wheat is broadly distributed rather than concentrated: everything in the 揚げ物 group is 唐揚げ or カツ, i.e. wheat coating in a shared fryer; the 焼きそば is a wheat noodle; the ホルモン焼き, 豚キムチ, レバニラ and あんかけ are all soy-seasoned. ⚠ The three 肉刺し raw-meat dishes and the 馬刺し are the items a coeliac would most want to be clean and they are exactly the ones served with a dipping sauce the shop does not name — ミノ刺し, 鳥刺し, センマイ刺し and 馬刺し all normally arrive with soy or a sesame-soy dare. Ask before dipping. ⚠ For a vegan the card is close to empty: 枝豆, 冷奴, 塩キャベツ, 茄子の一本漬け and 厚揚げ are the only plant items, and the pickle and the 厚揚げ are both routinely finished with soy or a dashi-based liquor.

tokyo_sekiyama_beikokuten.price_note: ⚠ PRICES ARE FROM 2016 AND HOT PEPPER SAYS SO. The page is stamped 関山米穀店 料理 2016/07/19 更新 and the listing carries ※更新日が2021/3/31以前の情報は、当時の価格及び税率に基づく情報となります — these figures predate the October 2019 rise to 10% consumption tax by more than three years. The dish list is still worth having because at a tapas bar the composition of the plates changes far more slowly than the prices. Instagram is the shop’s only listed channel and serves a login wall to this egress; Tabelog has served HTTP 403 to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ WHAT THIS PLACE IS: a Spanish-leaning bistro-bar near Jimbocho with a stock of natural wine — glasses from 700円, bottles from 3400円 — and a tapas list of about twenty-three plates. The name means “Sekiyama Rice Merchant”, which is what the premises used to be. ⚠ THE GLUTEN SHAPE IS UNUSUALLY GOOD, AND THAT IS THE USEFUL FINDING. Spanish small plates are mostly not built on flour: of the twenty-three dishes here, exactly one is bread (the loaf from Parlor Ekoda) and the rest are vegetables, cured meat, eggs, fish and rice. Two of the biggest plates are RICE — a brown-rice risotto with scallop and asparagus, and a mixed paella — which in most of this dataset is the thing that does not exist. That does not make them safe: a paella or risotto stock is a stock, and nobody has published what is in it. But the number of conversations you would need to have here is small. ⚠ THE VEGAN SHAPE IS THE OPPOSITE. Only two plates on the list contain no named animal — the marinated olives and the green salad — and the salad’s dressing is not described. Everything else is pork, poultry, offal, fish, cheese or egg. Nothing in this record has an allergen chart behind it; the flags below read the dish names and the shop’s own descriptions and nothing more.

items.ja: エビのカナッペ ゴイスアルギ風
items.en: Prawn canapé in the style of Goiz Argi — the shop names the San Sebastián pintxo bar it is copying, and sells this by the piece
items.note: カナッペ＝パンの上。A canapé is a thing on a piece of BREAD, so this is wheat by construction. Prawn, which is one of Japan’s eight statutory allergens.

items.ja: 黒トリュフのオムレツ
items.en: Black truffle omelette — the shop’s recommended main, soft egg with truffle worked through it
items.note: オムレツ自体は卵とバター＝小麦不使用。An omelette is egg and fat, with no wheat of its own — one of the better bets on a tapas list if you avoid gluten. Kept at ask because truffle products are frequently sold as a paste or oil whose carrier is not declared. Egg and dairy, so not vegan.

items.ja: パテ・ド・カンパーニュ
items.en: Country pâté — pork and chicken liver, the wine-bar default. Served immediately, so it is what to order first
items.note: パテは小麦粉やパン粉をつなぎに使う場合がある。Pork and chicken liver. Pâté is frequently bound with breadcrumbs or flour and sometimes finished with brandy — none of that is declared here — and it will arrive with bread unless you say otherwise.

items.en: Chicken white-liver pâté — made from the pale, fatty livers rather than ordinary ones
items.note: Poultry offal. Same binder question as the country pâté, and the same bread alongside.

リエット自体は豚肉と脂のみが基本。Rillettes are traditionally just pork and its own fat, which would make this wheat-free — but it is a spread, and it is served to be spread on something. Ask for it without the bread.

items.ja: パーラー江古田さんのパン
items.en: Bread from Parlor Ekoda — the shop names its baker rather than baking its own
items.note: THE ONE ITEM ON THE ENTIRE LIST MADE OF WHEAT, WHICH IS WORTH SAYING OUT LOUD ABOUT A EUROPEAN WINE BAR. Everything else here is vegetables, meat, fish, eggs or rice; this is the bread. Whether it contains dairy or egg depends on the loaf and is not stated.

items.en: Marinated olives — the cheapest plate on the list
items.note: ONE OF ONLY TWO PLATES HERE WITH NO NAMED ANIMAL IN IT. Olives, oil, herbs and usually garlic and citrus. No wheat ingredient and no animal ingredient. Kept at ask for gluten only because the marinade is not described and no allergen policy exists.

items.ja: 自然な葉っぱのグリーンサラダ
items.romaji: shizen na happa no gurīn sarada
items.en: Green salad of unforced leaves — the shop’s phrasing suggests small-grower salad rather than bagged
items.note: ドレッシング未掲載。The leaves are the dish and the dressing is the unknown. A Spanish bar’s default is oil and sherry vinegar, which would be both vegan and wheat-free; a Japanese kitchen’s default frequently is not. Ask, and ask whether cheese or anchovy goes on it.

items.ja: ブラウンマッシュルームだけのサラダ
items.en: A salad of nothing but brown mushrooms, raw and sliced
items.note: 「だけ」は具材の話でドレッシングの話ではない。The “nothing but” refers to what is in the bowl, not what is poured on it — raw mushroom salads in this idiom are almost always finished with shaved hard CHEESE and sometimes anchovy. Ask before assuming this is the plant plate.

items.ja: ブラータチーズとフルーツトマト
items.en: Burrata with intensively grown sweet tomatoes
items.note: Fresh cow’s-milk cheese, so dairy. No wheat ingredient in either component — one of the plates a coeliac can most likely eat here, subject to what it is served with.

items.ja: パタタス・ブラバス（スペイン風ポテトフライ）
items.en: Patatas bravas — fried potato under a spiced tomato sauce
items.note: ブラバスソース自体は小麦不使用が普通、ただしアイオリを添える店が多い＝卵。The potato and the brava sauce are normally wheat-free and plant-based; the standard Spanish service adds AIOLI, which is egg. The fryer is also shared with whatever else this kitchen fries. Ask for it without aioli if that matters.

items.ja: ホワイトアスパラのバター焼、ミモレットチーズがけ
items.romaji: howaito asupara no batā-yaki, mimoretto chīzu-gake
items.en: White asparagus cooked in butter with mimolette grated over
items.note: Butter and hard cheese, so dairy twice. No wheat ingredient.

items.ja: スペイン産サラミの盛り合わせ
items.note: サラミは小麦系のつなぎや燻製工程を含む場合がある。Cured pork. Salami is usually wheat-free but not reliably so — some use rusk or wheat-derived dextrose — and none of that is declared. Will arrive with bread unless you say otherwise.

items.ja: 砂肝のコンフィ、カレー風味
items.en: Chicken gizzard confit with curry spicing
items.note: ⚠「カレー風味」は要確認。Poultry offal cooked slowly in fat. The word “curry” is the thing to ask about: if the kitchen is using a Japanese curry powder or paste rather than whole spices, that is a WHEAT product. Curry spice powder itself normally is not.

items.ja: エビとマッシュルームのアヒージョ
items.en: Prawns and mushrooms in bubbling garlic oil
items.note: アヒージョ自体はオイル・にんにく・唐辛子＝小麦不使用。The dish itself is oil, garlic and chilli, with no wheat — but ahijo exists to be mopped up with bread and arrives with it. Prawn: statutory allergen.

items.en: Tandoori mackerel — the kitchen’s one obvious departure from Spain
items.note: タンドリーマリネは通常ヨーグルト＋スパイス＝乳製品。Mackerel, which is a declarable fish in Japan and a common histamine problem besides. A tandoori marinade is yoghurt and spice, so dairy; whether the spice mix carries a wheat carrier is not declared.

items.ja: 鶏セセリ肉のプランチャ（鉄板焼き）
items.en: Chicken neck meat on the plancha — seseri is the muscle from around the neck, chewy and prized in Japan
items.note: Chicken, grilled on a flat plate. Wheat only if the marinade or finishing sauce carries it, which is not stated. The plancha is shared with everything else grilled here.

items.ja: ラムの肉団子 トマト煮込み
items.note: ⚠ 肉団子はパン粉をつなぎに使うのが一般的。Lamb. Meatballs are normally bound with BREADCRUMBS, which is the most easily missed wheat on any European menu — ask specifically. Egg is a common second binder.

items.ja: 松坂ポークのロースト
items.en: Roast Matsusaka pork — the named-breed pork from Mie
items.note: Pork. A roast itself carries no wheat; a pan sauce may be flour-thickened and is not described.

items.en: Roast Aomori duck — the most expensive plate on the list
items.note: Duck. Same question about the sauce as the pork.

items.ja: ホタテとアスパラの玄米リゾット
items.romaji: hotate to asupara no genmai rizotto
items.en: Scallop and asparagus risotto made with BROWN rice rather than arborio — an unusual choice and a deliberate one
items.note: THE RICE DISHES ARE THE REASON A COELIAC MIGHT EAT HERE. 玄米＝小麦不使用、ただしブイヨンとチーズは未掲載。Brown rice carries no wheat at all. What is not published is the stock — a risotto is built on one — and whether it finishes with cheese and butter, which it almost certainly does. Scallop is a mollusc. Ask about the brodo.

items.en: Mixed paella — the sharing dish and the biggest plate on the list
items.note: パエリアは米＝小麦不使用、ただし出汁と具材は未掲載。Rice, saffron and stock — no flour anywhere in the construction, which is why paella is one of the safest European party dishes for a coeliac. “Mixed” means it will contain both seafood and meat, so shellfish is near-certain, and the stock is the one thing to ask about.

Dairy. Which cheeses is not published; blue cheeses are the one category where a wheat-based mould culture is occasionally used, and none of that is declared. Will come with bread or crackers unless you ask.

tokyo_taishu_sushi_sakaba_ronj.price_note: ⚠ THE BEST-SOURCED RECORD IN THIS TICK: an opening report in Shibuya Keizai Shimbun dated 2026.03.02, six days after the shop opened on 2026-02-26, listing named dishes at named prices. That is trade press quoting the operator, not a diner’s photograph, and it is six months old rather than six years. ⚠ WHO RUNS IT AND WHY THAT PREDICTS THE KITCHEN: the operator is For You (Toshima-ku), the company behind 十割蕎麦 嵯峨谷 and とんかつ わか葉 in Omotesandō Hills — soba and tonkatsu, i.e. no seafood experience — so for this new format it partnered with Dynac, who run 大衆すし酒場 めのじ in Yokohama’s Noge, and built Ronji on that template. The names are sushi-counter slang for numbers: めのじ is five, ろんじ is six. 17.5 tsubo over two floors, 42 seats, 道玄坂2 by Shibuya Mark City, 16:00–23:00 weekdays and from 12:00 at weekends and holidays. The stated average spend is 2,800円. ⚠ THE DIETARY PICTURE IS SIMPLE AND UNPROMISING. Half the menu is TEMPURA, which is wheat batter in shared oil with no exceptions, and the other half is sushi, which is fish with soy sauce. The one plate a vegetarian would look at, 生海苔揚げ出し豆腐, is fried tofu under a seaweed sauce thickened in dashi — the same trap as every agedashi in this dataset. The cheapest tempura pieces (kabocha at 99 yen, aubergine at 165) are vegetables, and they are vegetables in wheat batter fried in the oil that just cooked prawn and chicken. ⚠ ONE ITEM WORTH KNOWING ABOUT FOR A NON-DIETARY REASON: 太宰巻き is named for Dazai Osamu, because natto and salmon roe appear together in a passage of his HUMAN LOST. It is a literary joke you would otherwise eat without noticing. Instagram is the shop’s only listed channel and serves a login wall to this egress; Tabelog has served HTTP 403 to this egress since 2026-09-02.

items.en: Squid or octopus nigiri — the 99-yen entry point, and the price the shop leads with
items.note: 寿司飯は酢・砂糖・塩＝小麦不使用。つけ醤油が小麦。The rice is vinegared rice and the topping is raw mollusc — no wheat in either. The soy sauce is the wheat, and at a counter like this it is poured by you, so it is one of the few sushi orders you can control. Squid and octopus are molluscs, which matters separately from fish for shellfish allergies.
Raw fish on vinegared rice. Wheat only via the soy you add yourself — unless the piece arrives brushed with ニキリ, a reduced soy glaze, which some counters do without saying.
Sea snail — a mollusc. Same soy question as the rest of the counter.
Raw tuna on vinegared rice. Note that 赤身 is frequently served as ヅケ — marinated in soy — at cheap counters; if it arrives already dark, the wheat is inside it.

items.en: Eel-and-butter nigiri — grilled eel with butter, the most expensive single piece on the list
items.note: ⚠ 鰻の蒲焼のタレは醤油・味醂ベース＝小麦。バター＝乳。Grilled eel is glazed with a soy-and-mirin tare through the cooking, so the wheat is painted onto the fish rather than added at the table — this is the one nigiri on the list that cannot be ordered wheat-free. Butter adds dairy.

items.en: The five-piece “good fortune” selection — the shop’s set of five nigiri
items.note: Which five is not published and rotates with the daily buying. Assume at least one glazed or marinated piece in any set of five, which is where the wheat enters.

items.ja: 本日の刺し身 / 握り（毎日10〜15種類）
items.en: The daily fish — ten to fifteen kinds bought each day, available either as sashimi or as nigiri
items.note: Raw fish, cut to order. The interesting structural fact is that the same fish is sold both ways at very different prices — sashimi from 429 yen, the same thing on rice from 99. No wheat in the fish; the soy is yours to control.

items.en: Kabocha squash tempura — the 99-yen tempura, and the cheapest vegetable on the list
items.note: 天ぷらの衣は小麦粉、揚げ油は共用。THIS IS THE VEGETABLE THAT IS NOT A VEGETARIAN OPTION. The squash is plant food; the batter is wheat flour and egg, and the oil is the same oil that just fried prawn, whiting and chicken. At a 99-yen izakaya nothing is fried separately.
Same wheat-and-egg batter, same shared fryer. Tempura tsuyu is dashi and soy as well, so both the coating and the dip fail.

items.en: Daikon tempura steeped in shellfish stock before frying — one of the shop’s invented tempura
items.note: ⚠ 貝出汁を含ませた大根＝具材そのものが貝。THE TRAP TEMPURA. This looks like the plainest vegetable on the board and it is not one: the daikon has been soaked in SHELLFISH stock before it was battered, so the mollusc is inside the radish rather than beside it. Wheat batter on top of that.

items.ja: 半熟海苔たま天ですよ
items.en: Soft-boiled-egg tempura, which you break open and eat with a separate nori tempura — the shop’s showpiece and its silliest name
items.note: 卵の天ぷら＋海苔の天ぷら。Egg inside wheat batter, eaten with seaweed inside wheat batter. Egg, wheat, shared oil.

items.en: The six-piece tempura selection — prawn, whiting, chicken and three vegetables
items.note: ⚠ エビ＝特定原材料。The published composition names prawn (statutory allergen), kisu whiting, and chicken alongside three vegetables — so the “three vegetables” arrive on a plate with seafood and poultry fried in the same oil. Wheat batter throughout.

items.en: The “Dazai roll” — natto and salmon roe, named for the passage in Dazai Osamu’s HUMAN LOST where the two appear together. One of the shop’s あて巻き, rolls made to drink with
items.note: 納豆自体は大豆と納豆菌のみだが、付属のタレは醤油＋かつおだし、筋子は魚卵。The natto is the one clean component — soybeans and culture. The salmon roe is fish roe and is cured in soy, and the natto tare that goes into a roll like this is soy sauce with bonito extract. Wheat and fish, in a roll that reads as beans and rice.

items.ja: 煮穴子ポテトサラダ / 牛もつ煮込み
items.en: Two of the à la carte plates at one price: potato salad with simmered conger eel, and stewed beef offal
items.section: 一品・つまみ A la carte
items.note: 煮穴子は醤油ダレで煮る、もつ煮込みは味噌または醤油仕立て。⚠ THE POTATO SALAD IS NOT THE SAFE ONE — it has soy-simmered conger eel through it, so it is fish plus wheat plus the egg in the mayonnaise. The offal stew is beef tripe in a miso or soy braise: wheat or barley either way.

items.en: Agedashi tofu under a fresh-seaweed sauce — deep-fried tofu in a thickened green nori glaze
items.section: 一品・つまみ A la carte
items.note: THE ITEM A VEGETARIAN WILL ORDER, AND IT FAILS TWICE. 揚げ出しの衣は片栗粉でも、あんは鰹だし＋醤油。Tofu and seaweed are both plant food; the sauce poured over them is bonito dashi thickened and seasoned with soy sauce, so the animal content and the wheat are both in the liquid. The tofu is also fried in the tempura oil.

items.en: Draught beer from 495 yen, sake from 429 yen
items.price: ビール 495円～ / 日本酒 429円～
items.note: ビール＝大麦麦芽＝グルテン。日本酒＝米・米麹・水。Two opposite answers in one line: beer is barley malt and never gluten-free, sake is rice and koji and water and normally is. If you avoid gluten at this counter, drink the sake.

items.ja: ろんじ酎ハイ／レモン酎ハイ／ウーロンハイ（1杯目429円・2杯目319円・3杯目209円）
items.en: The house highballs, on a sliding scale that rewards staying: 429 yen for the first, 319 for the second, 209 for the third
items.note: 焼酎の原料（芋・麦・米）は未掲載。The descending price is the point and is worth knowing before you order one drink and leave. On gluten: the shochu base is not published and barley shochu is common. Also on the list is 角の「前」割り, Suntory Kaku whisky pre-mixed with water and rested 24 hours — whisky is distilled from malted BARLEY.
